subject: Re: Dedicated capacity vs hyperscaler GPU - follow-up and next tests
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-demo: Dedicated capacity vs hyperscaler evaluation — recap & proposed next tests

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap from our side and a proposed set of next tests so we can validate the decision criteria you listed on the call (cost/unit, sustained capacity, tail latency under production traffic patterns, and VPC/networking behaviour).

High-level recap:
- Goal: Determine whether Acme should use Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) or rely on hyperscaler GPU endpoints for production throughput.
- Key concerns you raised: capacity guarantees for sustained throughput, predictable unit cost at scale, integration into your VPC, and compliance/audit evidence.

Redwood differentiators (summary):
- Dedicated reserved capacity with explicit pool guarantees (we can reserve N GPUs for your account with predictable throughput and a defined SLA).
- Smart routing + automatic fallback: requests will failover to compatible instances or smaller model variants if capacity constraints occur, reducing error surface for end users.
- Workload-aware batching + KV/prefix caching to lower per-token cost while preserving tail latency SLOs.
- Security: VPC peering, customer-managed KMS integration, and exportable audit logs for SOC2/audit purposes.

Proposed technical tests (we recommend running these in the order below):
1) Integration sanity: deploy a small test service in your staging VPC and verify networking, auth, and KMS flows (1–2 days).
2) Sustained throughput test: 48-hour sustained run at your expected QPS (we suggested 1M tokens/day during the call) to validate capacity and cost profile.
3) Tail-latency bursts: synthetic burst tests to characterize p95/p99 behavior and cold-start implications.
4) Failure/fallback test: simulate capacity pressure and validate our automatic fallback/rollout behaviours.

Attachments: I attached a short comparison PDF and a draft mutual action plan that maps owners and dates for each step.

Next steps / ask:
- Can you confirm the primary technical contact for the integration (we heard Emily)?
- Are you comfortable with the proposed sustained test size (1M tokens/day) or should we size for a different target?
- If yes, we can provision a short dedicated trial pool and have Rishi loop in on pricing/contracting.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite with a short kickoff and the MAP.

—
Markus Klein
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Markus — very clear and helpful. A few quick clarifications from our side before we lock dates: 

- Pricing model: when you say "predictable unit cost", does that include egress and networking across the VPC peering, or is that separate? We're trying to compare fully loaded cost vs the hyperscaler.
- Capacity guarantees: does Redwood reserve physical GPUs for us, or is this a logical reservation across a pool that may be backfilled? Curious about how you handle noisy neighbors.
- Test size: 1M tokens/day is fine as a starting point, but we'd like to validate a 48-hour sustained run at that level plus a second test at 2x that load.

Also looping in our procurement lead (Emily) — she'll need an outline of the contract/commitment levels and a vendor onboarding checklist.

If you can send the MAP and a short pricing sketch, we can propose times for the kickoff.

—
Sara Lee
Head of ML Engineering, Acme AI

Hi Sara / Emily — thanks, agreed on next steps. Attaching the MAP and a short pricing sketch to give procurement a starting point (high level numbers only until we size the reservation).

Answering your questions:
- Pricing: the quote we shared is our inference unit cost (per 1k tokens) for the dedicated pool. Egress/networking costs are billed separately where applicable (same as hyperscalers) — we can surface an estimate for your networking profile as part of the MAP.
- Capacity guarantees: Redwood Dedicated reserves capacity as a combination of logical reservations backed by capacity pools that we size per-customer. For larger committed pools we do physical GPU allocation to reduce noisy-neighbor risk and provide stronger throughput consistency. The SLA and isolation level scale with commitment.

Proposed kickoff + tests (dates are tentative):
- 2026-05-18: Integration sanity / VPC + KMS verification (Emily / your infra + Laura from our side)
- 2026-05-20 to 2026-05-22: 48-hour sustained run at 1M tokens/day (primary test)
- 2026-05-24: Burst/p99 characterization and failure/fallback test

Ownership (draft MAP):
- Acme: provide test dataset, primary technical contact (Emily), and procurement scope (Emily)
- Redwood: provision short-term dedicated trial pool, run tests with monitoring enabled, provide streaming logs and audit events

Attachments included: redwood-dedicated-vs-hyperscaler-comparison.pdf; ACME-MAP-DRAFT.xlsx (link to MAP: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/redwood-acme-map)

If that looks good I’ll send calendar invites and we’ll provision the trial capacity. Rishi — can you share a draft reserved-capacity pricing table (ballpark) so Emily can start internal approvals?

Emily / Sara — looping in on pricing/contracting. Quick ballpark to help procurement:
- Small reserved pool (4 x A100-equivalent GPUs) — ~$18k/mo committed (12-month minimum) — expected steady-state inference cost ~ $0.012 / 1k tokens (model dependent).
- Medium reserved pool (16 x A100-equivalent) — ~$64k/mo committed — ~ $0.009 / 1k tokens at scale.
- For short trials we can do a 30-day trial reservation with prorated billing and reduced onboarding paperwork; pricing above is indicative.

SLA & capacity notes: for medium+ pools we can provide stronger isolation and a 99.9% availability SLA for the inference runtime and a capacity-pinning option to reduce cold-start variance. Full SLA language and any exceptions would be in the contract addendum.

If you share Emily's procurement checklist I can have legal add the required vendor items and a draft order form.

—
